BiblicalUsage: Bidkar means with a stab, and he is named once, as Jehu's captain. In 2 Kings 9:25 Jehu tells Bidkar to take up Joram's body and cast it in the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, remembering how they rode together when the Lord laid this burden on Ahab. A captain carrying out a king's sentence on the very ground where Naboth died.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bidkar's single verse is a reminder that God's word against Ahab waited years, and then fell in a day.
